source.title: Connecting the Dots between Audio and Text without Parallel Data through Visual Knowledge Transfer
source.authors: Yanpeng Zhao; Jack Hessel; Youngjae Yu; Ximing Lu; Rowan Zellers; Yejin Choi

record.tranche_reason: Reports an empirical scaling relationship for audio-text fine-tuning, an audio setting outside language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the performance-versus-number-of-paired-audio-caption-examples experiments in Figure 7. Other audio retrieval and classification results compare model variants or curation methods, not scaling in the sense of the claim, so they are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (audio-text contrastive fine-tuning of a CLIP-initialised audio encoder), the study varies the number of gold AudioCaps pairs from 0 to 2^16. It reports downstream retrieval and zero-shot classification rising roughly linearly in log pair count, then extrapolates that trend. This bears on V6 only. It measures no loss, so it cannot speak to V5's power-law loss form.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Zero-shot performance grows roughly linearly with the log of supervised audio-caption pairs, which the authors liken to Kaplan et al. They estimate about 2^21 (about 2M) pairs would reach ESC50 human parity (81%), while noting the extrapolation's reliability is unclear.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies paired audio-caption fine-tuning data and measures audio retrieval and classification performance; it does not sweep language-model parameters, tokens, or training compute or measure held-out loss.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance changes with the number of supervised audio-caption pairs used for fine-tuning.
record.peer_reviewed: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The scaling results are presented as curves without extractable point values or uncertainty estimates. The authors describe the trend as rough and explicitly question the reliability of extrapolation.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported audio retrieval, classification, and fine-tuning comparisons were omitted because they do not vary scale for the claim-relevant results; see Tables 3-4 and Appendix E.

untested.parts: No language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No fitted law is checked against larger runs; the 2M-pair estimate is never verified.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
No loss measured and no power-law fit. Only downstream metrics versus fine-tuning pair count, described as log-linear.
No model-size or pretraining-loss scaling; only amount of fine-tuning supervision. No fitted function or error bars on the curves.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: VAT versus AT fine-tuning curves over the same 0 to 2^16 pair sweep, on ESC50 zero-shot accuracy and AudioCaps Text-to-Audio R@1. These do vary scale, contrary to rows_left_out.
With only 442 gold pairs, AT retrieval matches the CLIP image-text oracle (OracleAV-CLIP: 4.8/6.6 R@1).

record.verdict_notes: The scaling evidence is a side analysis in a paper on pivot-based audio-text alignment. Curves are figure-only and descriptive, with no fitted law. The analogy to Kaplan is about downstream metric versus log data, not loss power laws, so V5 is left untested rather than supported.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation of language-model loss laws from small runs to larger runs.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.

The study tests an audio setting by varying paired audio-caption supervision and measuring retrieval and classification performance; it does not test held-out pretraining loss, image/video model scaling, repeated data, or transfer and fine-tuning regimes beyond this setup.
Tests downstream audio-task performance against the amount of paired audio-caption supervision, not against model parameter count or pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitting choices or exponents, or test whether curves bend away from power laws.

rows.subject: vip-AnT fine-tuned on gold AudioCaps audio-caption pairs (GC)
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned on gold AudioCaps audio-caption pairs
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of gold AudioCaps pairs used for audio-text fine-tuning.
rows.note: The text reports that more aligned pairs improve retrieval and that zero-shot performance is roughly linear in the log of the number of supervised pairs. It also says 442 pairs give AT alignment as strong as VT alignment; the figure does not provide extractable values for this specific curve.
rows.check: Unlink V5: the measure is downstream R@1 and the trend is log-linear, not a loss power law. Baseline at 0 pairs is vip-AnT 0.8 R@1 (Table 3); the full 44K GC endpoint is 27.7 R@1. The variable is fine-tuning data, not model or pretraining scale.

rows.note: The text reports roughly linear performance growth with the log of the number of supervised pairs. It estimates that about 2^21 ≈ 2M pairs would be needed to reach the stated ESC50 human-parity accuracy of 81%, while cautioning that the extrapolation's reliability is unclear.
rows.check: Unlink V5. Baseline at 0 pairs is 57.1% accuracy; the full GC endpoint is 69.5% (Table 4). The 2^21 pairs to reach 81% is an extrapolation the authors call of unclear reliability, not an observed value.

relationships.condition: vip-AnT audio encoder AT-fine-tuned on 0 to 2^16 gold AudioCaps pairs; AudioCaps retrieval and ESC50/US8K zero-shot classification
relationships.reason: Performance rises monotonically and 'roughly linear' in log pair count on all four curves (r1-r4), though only with fine-tuning data, not model scale.
relationships.display_finding: All four performance curves increased monotonically and roughly linearly with log paired-data size, demonstrating fine-tuning data scaling rather than model scaling.
